title: blockworld: a block-level geology-ecology sandbox for feasibility decisions
description:
A sandbox in which a site is discretised into blocks, each holding a replaceable layered geological column, and an intervention (ground replacement, dewatering, vegetation change, local gravity) is scored against explicit feasibility criteria: bearing capacity, settlement, slope stability, lander footpad capacity and ecological sustainability.

The package is organised around one question: does replacing a component flip the verdict, and how stable is that answer under uncertain inputs? A Study takes a site (DEM, boreholes, climate), a criteria set and a list of serialisable interventions, and returns per-criterion verdicts with normalised margins plus the flips induced by each intervention.

Deterministic formulas are replaceable through a registry, so an external numerical model (PLAXIS, FLAC3D) can supply the bearing capacity or the whole verifier without touching the rest of the pipeline. Uncertainty is reported as a probability of failure from Monte Carlo sampling and as a Morris elementary-effects screening ranking, rather than as a single factor of safety.

Contents: the blockworld Python package (site, geology, materials, hydrology, vegetation, animals, verifiers, edits, study API, uncertainty, reports, CLI), 69 tests, a data template, an example study configuration, and the scripts that regenerate every figure. All physical formulas are cited in the documentation; the parameters of the ecological and hydrological processes are explicitly order-of-magnitude settings and are labelled as such, and synthetic sites are marked synthetic in provenance so they are never presented as measurements.
